descriptions.Armenians: Armenians combine early infantry upgrades with a durable late-game foot army. Champions strengthened by Fereters and Halberdiers hold the front while Composite Bowmen punish heavily armored targets; Warrior Priests help preserve surviving infantry between fights. Use that formation to contest ground and protect Trebuchets rather than chasing cavalry across the map. Their reinforced galley line also rewards investment on water, while mobile ranged armies and enemy siege demand careful positioning on land.
descriptions.Aztecs: Aztecs reward active infantry and Monk play, using faster military production to maintain pressure. Eagle Warriors raid and reach vulnerable ranged units, while Monks contest relics and discourage expensive cavalry; add Pikemen when you need a cheaper screen. Garland Wars strengthens the late-game infantry army, with Jaguar Warriors serving as a specialist answer to enemy infantry. Siege Rams or Siege Onagers help break defended positions, but limited naval options make prolonged water games less comfortable.
descriptions.Bengalis: Bengalis build toward a durable army supported by their extra villagers on advancing ages. Rathas offer a mobile core that can switch between ranged and melee combat, while Elephant Archers or Battle Elephants suit slower pushes with a strong economy behind them. Halberdiers, Skirmishers, and armored Monks help protect those expensive units. Preserve your army and advance with siege rather than trading elephants carelessly into massed anti-cavalry units or conversions.
descriptions.Berbers: Berbers excel at mobile pressure with discounted stable units. Knights and Camel Riders give an efficient Castle Age army, developing into Cavalier or Heavy Camel Riders according to the opposing composition. Camel Archers add mobile ranged damage, especially against cavalry archers, while Hussars raid and screen for them. Use speed to take favorable fights and replenish losses; add Hand Cannoneers or siege when infantry and fortified positions stop your cavalry from making progress.
descriptions.Bohemians: Bohemians favor methodical pushes built around Halberdiers, gunpowder, and siege. Castle Age Chemistry opens an early Hand Cannoneer option, while Houfnice become the centerpiece of a late-game army that can threaten enemy siege and fortifications. Hussite Wagons can reinforce the formation, and Monks offer another answer to costly mounted units. Keep the army together and protect its flanks: chasing raids with their limited cavalry is less effective than controlling the ground your opponent needs.
descriptions.Britons: Britons win space with long-range foot archers. Build a Crossbowman mass into Arbalesters or Longbowmen, using Halberdiers to discourage cavalry from closing the distance and Skirmishers when an archer war demands them. Warwolf Trebuchets let a protected ranged army turn map control into a siege push. Preserve the archer mass and fight from prepared positions; fast flanks, rams, and enemy siege are dangerous when your frontline or vision breaks down.
descriptions.Bulgarians: Bulgarians use inexpensive upgrade transitions to keep melee pressure moving. Their free militia-line upgrades support an early infantry opening, then Knights, Konniks, or Hussars become central once Stirrups is available. Kreposts provide forward positions and Konnik production, while Halberdiers and siege support the push. Bagains makes Two-Handed Swordsmen useful in prolonged melee fights, but the weak foot-archer progression means you should plan another answer to ranged armies rather than relying on a late archer switch.
descriptions.Burgundians: Burgundians turn early economic upgrades and discounted stable technologies into cavalry timing attacks. Castle Age Cavalier and an accessible Paladin upgrade can create pressure before an opponent finishes their own transitions, while Coustilliers reward charging, withdrawing, and charging again. Hand Cannoneers and Bombard Cannons give the cavalry useful support against infantry and defenses. Balance investment in the economy with enough military to survive; researching upgrades early is valuable only if you can reach the fighting window safely.
descriptions.Burmese: Burmese combine strong melee infantry with cavalry, Monks, and siege. Arambai can deliver concentrated damage from behind a screen, while Champions and Halberdiers benefit from the civilization's infantry attack bonus. Hussars or armored Battle Elephants offer different ways to apply pressure, and Bombard Cannons help dismantle fortified positions. Free wood upgrades support the transition, but weaker ranged armor makes a prolonged skirmisher duel unattractive; use cavalry, siege, or positioning to deal with enemy archers.
descriptions.Byzantines: Byzantines adapt through inexpensive counter units rather than committing to one expensive army immediately. Halberdiers, Elite Skirmishers, and Camel Riders let you answer the opponent while strong buildings and a cheaper Imperial advance buy time. Add Arbalesters, gunpowder, or siege to turn that defense into pressure; Cataphracts are a powerful but costly specialist against infantry. Their Fire Ships also support water control. Keep matching your composition to the threat instead of expecting every available unit to excel in direct fights.
descriptions.Celts: Celts are strongest when fast infantry protects a dangerous siege army. Halberdiers screen against cavalry, while Woad Raiders threaten exposed ranged units and raid away from the main push. Faster-firing Siege Onagers and Heavy Scorpions punish packed armies, and durable Siege Rams help force entry into defended bases. Their wood economy supports sustained production. Keep siege protected and use infantry speed to secure flanks; a scattered army loses much of the strength of this combination.
descriptions.Chinese: Chinese reward a strong economy and deliberate switches between complementary units. Arbalesters or Chu Ko Nu provide ranged damage, with Halberdiers, Skirmishers, or Cavalier chosen to cover the opponent's response. Discounted technologies make those transitions easier, while Rocketry-supported siege offers another route against massed armies. Avoid buying several complete armies at once: establish a main damage source, add the counter it needs, and use siege to convert a favorable fight into lasting map control.
descriptions.Cumans: Cumans can invest in a second Feudal Age Town Center or use early siege access to pressure an opponent. Once the economy is established, fast cavalry and Kipchaks support raids, flanks, and quick changes of direction; Hussars, Paladins, or Steppe Lancers can form the melee component. Siege Rams help turn mobility into damage against a base. The second Town Center is a commitment, so scout pressure carefully and do not assume a booming economy can defend itself.
descriptions.Danes: Danes favor infantry-led attacks backed by siege. Jomsvikings can fight on land and throw torches at buildings or ships, while faster Varangian Guards help keep pressure on a retreating army. Halberdiers protect the formation from cavalry, and Siege Onagers with Northmen's Fury strengthen a committed push. Hamask rewards infantry that remains in combat as it loses health, but does not make reckless losses worthwhile. Longships offer a mobile option on water; limited cavalry upgrades make chasing land raids harder.
descriptions.Dravidians: Dravidians build effective foot armies around Arbalesters, fast-firing Skirmishers, and Halberdiers. Wootz Steel gives Champions and Urumi Swordsmen a way through heavily armored melee opponents, while Elephant Archers provide a more expensive ranged option when the economy can support them. Siege and Bombard Cannons help a protected formation advance. Their fishing bonuses and Thirisadai make water relevant too, but limited cavalry makes it important to defend against raids and avoid being pulled apart on open maps.
descriptions.Ethiopians: Ethiopians turn age-up resources and fast-firing archers into strong attack windows. Crossbowmen and Arbalesters are the usual damage core, with the free Pikeman upgrade easing protection against cavalry. Later, Torsion Engines gives siege a major role against packed formations, while Shotel Warriors can punish an exposed economy or reinforce an urgent attack. Keep the ranged army protected and add siege as defenses grow; the speed of Shotels does not make them a substitute for a durable frontline.
descriptions.Franks: Franks offer a direct cavalry plan, using their food economy and extra cavalry health to support Scouts into Knights and Paladins. Cheaper Castles secure forward ground and produce Throwing Axemen to remove the infantry that obstructs a cavalry push. Halberdiers cover opposing cavalry, while Bombard Cannons and Trebuchets handle defenses. Keep producing and upgrading your main mounted army, but switch support when counters appear rather than repeatedly charging Paladins into a prepared spear wall.
descriptions.Georgians: Georgians favor sustained cavalry pressure supported by a well-positioned economy. Monaspa become more threatening in groups, while regenerating mounted units reward withdrawing damaged troops and returning to fight again. Fortified Churches support nearby villagers, and hill positions strengthen defense while the army gathers. Add Halberdiers against enemy cavalry or siege against a protected infantry mass. Avoid splitting your Monaspa into ineffective fragments or treating regeneration as protection against a decisive counterattack.
descriptions.Goths: Goths win through infantry production and the right mix of inexpensive units. Huskarls close on archers, Halberdiers counter cavalry, and Champions handle many infantry and low-gold fights; Anarchy and Perfusion let Barracks replace losses rapidly. Build enough economy and production to keep that flood going, with siege or gunpowder support when needed. Huskarls do not solve every matchup: specialist anti-infantry units and siege can punish a single-unit army, especially before the Goth economy reaches full production.
descriptions.Gurjaras: Gurjaras build mobile counter armies around Camel Riders and Shrivamsha Riders. Camels deal with cavalry, while Shrivamshas threaten exposed ranged units and raid; Chakram Throwers help when the opponent switches to dense infantry formations. Elephant Archers offer a sturdier but less mobile ranged alternative. Read the opposing composition and combine counters instead of using camels as general-purpose heavy cavalry. Massed spears and a protected siege line require a different approach from an open cavalry battle.
descriptions.Hindustanis: Hindustanis use cheaper villagers to support a flexible army of specialized counters. Imperial Camel Riders answer mounted armies, Ghulams threaten foot archers, and long-range Hand Cannoneers deal with infantry behind a protective screen. Hussars add raiding pressure, while Bombard Cannons help the main army advance through defenses. Choose the specialist that matches the threat: camels are not a replacement for Knights in every fight, and isolated gunpowder units still need protection from fast attackers.
descriptions.Huns: Huns keep pressure moving with cavalry and discounted cavalry archers, helped by an economy that never needs Houses. Heavy Cavalry Archers with Hussars form a mobile late-game army, while Knights into Paladins offer a direct melee route. Tarkans are useful when piercing defenses and damaging buildings matters more than winning a straight cavalry duel. Raid, preserve the ranged mass, and attack from several directions; Siege Rams and Trebuchets become important when the opponent stops offering open-field fights.
descriptions.Incas: Incas assemble complementary foot units rather than relying on conventional cavalry. Kamayuks fight effectively in a compact formation and help stop mounted armies, Slingers answer infantry, and Skirmishers or Arbalesters provide ranged support. Champi Warriors give another way to pressure exposed units and an opponent's economy. Military discounts help sustain the mix, with siege needed to break fortified ground. Protect your ranged support and choose engagements carefully; a dense formation is useful in melee but vulnerable to siege shots.
descriptions.Italians: Italians combine efficient age advances with flexible ranged armies and strong water options. Arbalesters provide a practical core, while Genoese Crossbowmen are particularly useful against cavalry. Discounted Hand Cannoneers and Bombard Cannons support an Imperial push, and Condottieri offer a mobile infantry response to gunpowder. On water, cheaper Fishing Ships and dock technologies help build momentum. Preserve a ranged mass and screen it well; specialized anti-cavalry archers still need help against siege and enemy foot archers.
descriptions.Japanese: Japanese use efficient early gathering buildings and fast-attacking infantry to support several army paths. Arbalesters or Heavy Cavalry Archers can provide ranged damage, with Halberdiers screening cavalry and Champions handling prolonged infantry fights. Samurai are a specialist choice against suitable unique units rather than an automatic answer to every army. Kataparuto Trebuchets help a protected force push or reposition quickly. Their durable, productive Fishing Ships also make hybrid maps attractive, but the main land army still needs protection from siege.
descriptions.Jurchens: Jurchens combine aggressive cavalry with explosive ranged support. Iron Pagodas, Steppe Lancers, or Hussars can pressure the front and flanks while Grenadiers and Rocket Carts punish tightly packed targets. Halberdiers help screen opposing cavalry, and Bombard Cannons provide a separate answer to fortifications and siege. Choose a manageable mix and protect the expensive ranged units: the cavalry's attack speed encourages pressure, but unsupported charges into anti-cavalry formations can leave the gunpowder army exposed.
descriptions.Khitans: Khitans can apply pressure with early melee attack upgrades or take advantage of Castle Age Heavy Cavalry Archers. Hussars and Steppe Lancers provide mobility, while Heavy Camel Riders answer cavalry and Liao Dao give an infantry option for sustained fighting. Rocket Carts and Mounted Trebuchets support pushes when mobility alone cannot break a position. Build around one of those plans rather than researching every branch; the value of their melee bonuses depends on actually reaching and holding an engagement.
descriptions.Khmer: Khmer turn a flexible build order and strong farming economy into cavalry or siege pressure. Hussars are useful for raiding and screening, while Battle Elephants offer a costly frontline for a committed push. Heavy Scorpions and Ballista Elephants become dangerous against packed armies with Double Crossbow, supported by Halberdiers when enemy cavalry threatens. Keep vision and protect the siege mass; elephants are an investment to preserve, especially when the opponent can field Monks and large numbers of anti-cavalry units.
descriptions.Koreans: Koreans favor protected ranged armies and control of defended positions. War Wagons provide durable ranged damage, with Halberdiers screening cavalry and Arbalesters offering a cheaper core. Rocket Carts punish packed targets, while Bombard Cannons challenge siege and fortifications. Towers help secure the army's position, and Turtle Ships support deliberate naval pushes. Keep heavy ranged units screened and avoid being surrounded; their durability does not remove the need to answer enemy siege.
descriptions.Lithuanians: Lithuanians use early food and relic control to support a cavalry-centered game. Knights and Leitis benefit from secured relics, with Paladins offering a general heavy-cavalry route and Leitis attacking through melee armor. Fast-moving spears and Skirmishers help protect the economy while Monks contest the map. Winged Hussars add raids and a lower-gold frontline later. Relics strengthen the plan but are contested resources, so do not delay necessary army production while chasing an ideal cavalry bonus.
descriptions.Magyars: Magyars pressure early with discounted Scouts and free melee attack upgrades, then can transition into a strong mobile ranged army. Heavy Cavalry Archers with Recurve Bow supply late-game damage, while Hussars or Magyar Huszars screen, raid, and threaten enemy siege. Paladins are another option when a direct cavalry fight suits the matchup. Their strongest compositions require time and upgrades, so use early pressure to create room rather than expecting an economic bonus to carry a passive transition.
descriptions.Malay: Malay use fast age advances to create timing advantages and reach a broad infantry-and-archer army. Arbalesters with Halberdiers form a practical core, while discounted Battle Elephants can add pressure when an opponent is unprepared. Karambit Warriors reward mass and mobility, and Forced Levy gives Two-Handed Swordsmen a useful role when gold runs low. Strong fishing infrastructure supports water play. Avoid treating cheap elephants or numerous Karambits as individually durable units; they still need favorable fights and support.
descriptions.Malians: Malians can open with flexible foot armies and transition into hard-hitting cavalry. Extra pierce armor helps their Barracks units approach archers, while Farimba gives Cavalier, Heavy Camel Riders, and Light Cavalry a stronger late-game role. Gbetos supply mobile ranged melee damage but need a screen, and Bombard Cannons help close out a push. Use the wood savings and gold economy to support a focused transition; powerful individual options do not remove the need to answer the opponent's counter units.
descriptions.Mapuche: Mapuche combine mobile Kona and Bolas Riders with durable foot counters. Halberdiers protect against cavalry, while Skirmishers and Slingers support fights against archers and infantry; Malon adds pass-through damage to their ranged support. Settlements help produce the counter units needed to hold ground while mounted forces raid or flank. Keep the two parts working together: chasing with every mounted unit can leave the slower army exposed, while committing entirely to foot units gives up useful mobility.
descriptions.Mayans: Mayans build sustained pressure with discounted foot archers and an economy whose resources last longer. Arbalesters offer efficient massed damage, while Plumed Archers trade some production convenience for durability and mobility. Eagle Warriors raid and reach vulnerable ranged units, with Halberdiers covering cavalry and Siege Rams forcing entry into bases. Preserve the archer mass while threatening another angle with infantry. Without cavalry or gunpowder, the right mix of archers, Eagles, counters, and siege matters more than a single-unit flood.
descriptions.Mongols: Mongols use their hunting economy for early pressure and aim for a mobile late-game army. Mangudai and Hussars combine ranged damage, raiding, and protection against exposed siege, while Steppe Lancers offer another timing option. Drill lets Siege Rams and Siege Onagers move with the army instead of slowing every attack. The complete composition is expensive to assemble, so keep early units alive and contest resources. Avoid trapping the ranged mass where enemy cavalry or siege can force an unfavorable fight.
descriptions.Muisca: Muisca support ranged pressure with mobile infantry and Monks. Arbalesters benefit from Herbalism's speed, Champi Warriors can screen or raid, and Guecha Warriors offer another ranged option. Slingers answer infantry, while Pikemen and conversions help against mounted threats; healing near Settlements rewards preserving units between engagements. Temple Guards and siege can reinforce a more deliberate push. Keep the army's supporting pieces together, since extra melee armor does not make ranged units safe when surrounded or caught by siege.
descriptions.Persians: Persians use a growing economy to support a broad stable army. Knights into Savar provide a durable main force, Heavy Camel Riders answer cavalry, and Hussars raid or absorb attacks for ranged support. Kamandaran makes Crossbowmen useful without spending gold, while Hand Cannoneers and Bombard Cannons help against infantry and defenses. War Elephants are a powerful but expensive situational commitment. Favor mobility and complementary units unless you can protect elephants from Monks and massed anti-cavalry counters.
descriptions.Poles: Poles turn farming and stone income into sustained military production. Szlachta Privileges makes repeated Knight and Cavalier production affordable, while Winged Hussars offer a strong raiding and low-gold option later. Obuchs reduce enemy armor and pair well with ranged support, with Bombard Cannons or Siege Rams helping a push through defenses. Win through production, timing, and combined armies rather than expecting discounted cavalry to have every defensive upgrade; exposed farms and ranged counters still require careful protection.
descriptions.Portuguese: Portuguese stretch their gold through flexible ranged and gunpowder armies. Arbalesters are an accessible core, while Organ Guns and Hand Cannoneers offer alternatives against infantry-heavy opponents, supported by Halberdiers and Bombard Cannons. Arquebus improves gunpowder tracking and rewards preserving a protected firing line. Their ship bonuses and Caravels also support water play. Commit to the damage source the matchup needs instead of buying every gold unit at once, and protect slow gunpowder formations from raids and flanking attacks.
descriptions.Romans: Romans combine an efficient economy with armored infantry and inexpensive Scorpions. Legionaries or Halberdiers protect the ranged siege, while Centurions support the infantry and offer a mounted component for the army. Ballistas makes a preserved Scorpion mass increasingly threatening, and Siege Rams help turn favorable fights into damage against buildings. Keep the formation supported and moving toward an objective; enemy siege and attacks from several directions are more troublesome than the packed melee fights this army prefers.
descriptions.Saracens: Saracens use their market and broad military options to create sharp transitions. Arbalesters can pressure early, Heavy Camel Riders punish cavalry, and Mamelukes provide a more expensive mobile answer to mounted armies. Hussars screen and raid, while Siege Onagers, Siege Rams, or Bombard Cannons let you choose how to break a defended position. Trade at the market to reach a useful timing, then build an economy that sustains it; repeatedly buying resources is not a substitute for production behind the attack.
descriptions.Saxons: Saxons build around efficient foot armies and controlled ground. Hearth Troops open combat with javelins before joining the melee, while Champions, Varangian Guards, and Halberdiers offer different frontline roles. Arbalesters or Heavy Mounted Crossbowmen add ranged support. Additional Town Centers and Castles improve foot-soldier discounts, and Shield Wall rewards grouped infantry. Advance with siege and protect your formation, but spread or reposition when enemy siege makes a tightly packed army a liability.
descriptions.Shu: Shu favor a combined army of archers, infantry, and mobile siege. Discounted archer upgrades support Crossbowmen into Arbalesters, while White Feather Guards and Halberdiers form a protective line strengthened by Coiled Serpent Array. Bolt Magazine improves the ranged component, with War Chariots offering an additional option. Faster siege helps maintain pressure after winning ground. Keep the frontline and ranged units working together; bonuses that reward a formation do not remove its vulnerability to siege or attacks from several directions.
descriptions.Sicilians: Sicilians can pressure through fortified positions with Serjeants and Donjons or develop a cavalry army around Hauberk Cavalier. Reduced bonus damage makes ordinary counters less punishing, while Halberdiers and ranged support still help against specialized enemy armies. Siege Rams and Trebuchets turn a secure forward position into a push. Commit to a coherent approach and support it with production; resistance to bonus damage is not immunity, and Serjeants still need help catching mobile ranged units.
descriptions.Slavs: Slavs convert a strong farming economy into infantry, cavalry, and discounted siege. Knights or Boyars can lead a mobile phase, while Champions and Halberdiers become dangerous in massed melee fights after Druzhina. Siege Onagers and Siege Rams give a foot army the tools to break a defended position, with Hussars raiding elsewhere. Favor sustained production and combined pushes; limited late-game ranged options make it important to protect siege and avoid chasing faster armies with infantry alone.
descriptions.Spanish: Spanish create pressure with mobile Conquistadors, supported by Monks or Missionaries and a frontline suited to the opponent. Their late-game options include Paladins, Hussars, Halberdiers, and Elite Skirmishers, while Hand Cannoneers and Bombard Cannons support slower pushes. Faster building helps establish forward positions, and the trade bonus matters in team games. Preserve the expensive gunpowder units and choose their support carefully; the lack of a Crossbowman upgrade makes a conventional foot-archer progression a poor long-term plan.
descriptions.Tatars: Tatars build around cavalry archers and favorable terrain. Free ranged technologies support a transition to Heavy Cavalry Archers, with Hussars or Keshiks screening and raiding; Steppe Lancers offer another mobile attack option. Silk Armor improves the durability of key mounted units, while long-range Trebuchets help convert map control into a push. Fight from hills and preserve the ranged mass. Avoid being forced into prolonged infantry battles or letting a compact cavalry-archer group take an unprotected siege hit.
descriptions.Teutons: Teutons favor deliberate advances with heavily armored melee units and protected siege. Paladins provide a mounted route, while Champions, Halberdiers, or Teutonic Knights can hold the frontline for Siege Onagers and Bombard Cannons. Cheap farms help sustain those food-heavy armies, and Monks provide healing and conversion support. Teutonic Knights are especially useful when the enemy must fight in close quarters; their durability does not solve slow movement, so guard the flanks and avoid chasing mobile ranged armies.
descriptions.Tupi: Tupi combine foot archers and infantry in armies that can keep applying pressure. Arbalesters provide a conventional ranged core, while Blackwood Archers offer a more fragile alternative; Curare adds poison damage to foot-archer attacks. Champi Warriors and Slingers benefit from Caciques, with Halberdiers protecting against cavalry and Ibirapema Warriors offering area damage in melee. Cost refunds soften losses but do not make bad trades worthwhile. Protect the archers and bring siege when a defended position stops the advance.
descriptions.Turks: Turks build dangerous gunpowder armies with Janissaries or Hand Cannoneers protected by Hussars. Free Chemistry helps the Imperial transition, and Artillery gives Bombard Cannons extra reach for siege fights. Sipahi-supported Heavy Cavalry Archers offer a mobile alternative, while Heavy Camel Riders can answer cavalry. Secure gold and preserve the expensive damage dealers: without Pikeman or Elite Skirmisher upgrades, Turks cannot fall back on the same inexpensive counter mix as many other civilizations when resources run low.
descriptions.Varangians: Varangians combine durable mounted units with useful infantry and naval support. Jarls reduce enemy armor with ranged melee attacks, helping Cavalier or other melee units finish engagements; stronger Bloodlines supports the mounted army. Faster-attacking Varangian Guards offer an infantry route, while Halberdiers and Heavy Mounted Crossbowmen cover different threats. Their faster-firing Longships reward water investment. Keep support close enough to exploit the Jarls' attacks, and do not let costly cavalry become trapped in massed anti-cavalry units.
descriptions.Vietnamese: Vietnamese are comfortable building ranged armies that survive longer in archer fights. Rattan Archers resist incoming arrows, Arbalesters benefit from extra health, and Imperial Skirmishers provide an economical answer to opposing ranged units. Halberdiers screen cavalry, while Bombard Cannons help handle enemy siege; Battle Elephants offer a much heavier frontline when resources allow. Use knowledge of the enemy's starting location and efficient economic upgrades to plan pressure, but avoid letting a slow ranged army become surrounded.
descriptions.Vikings: Vikings use free economic upgrades to support strong infantry-and-archer timings. Arbalesters can lead an Imperial attack, while high-health Champions, regenerating Berserks, and Varangian Guards offer different ways to sustain melee pressure. Pikemen help screen cavalry, and Siege Rams turn an infantry push into damage against buildings. Discounted warships and Longships make water control a central strength on suitable maps. Preserve the economic lead and choose engagements carefully; limited cavalry makes answering raids and chasing mobile armies less straightforward.
descriptions.Wei: Wei favor mobile armies built around Xianbei Raiders and heavy cavalry. Hei-Kuang Cavalry or Tiger Cavalry can lead the melee component, with Hussars raiding and Halberdiers covering opposing mounted threats. Economic technologies add villagers, while discounted Traction Trebuchets help turn a growing economy into siege pressure. Ming Guang Armor strengthens mounted units in melee, but does not remove the need to respect anti-cavalry counters. Keep the ranged and melee components coordinated rather than committing the expensive frontline alone.
descriptions.Wu: Wu use regenerating infantry to support repeated pressure and preserve an army between fights. Jian Swordsmen and Halberdiers can form the front, with Arbalesters or long-range Fire Archers behind them; Fire Archers also threaten buildings and ships. Traction Trebuchets gain a larger role after Sitting Tiger, while naval bonuses support attacks on water. Advance with a protected ranged-and-siege group, and withdraw damaged infantry when possible; regeneration is less valuable if you lose the whole formation in one engagement.
